note: One deciding module per rule. Every other site delegates.
Where a second implementation is genuinely required, it is registered here
with a comparator that runs both over the same input, and with a mutation
that the comparator MUST fail on. A comparator that has never disagreed with
anything is unverified in exactly the way the [] / [] checker was.
Vectors derive from the SPEC, not from the implementation. The [] / []
inversion survived review because the checker's own vectors encoded the same
guess it did — a cross-check cannot catch two implementations inheriting one
wrong assumption through shared vectors. So `vectors` must cite `spec`.
Unregistered duplicates are not caught by CI. They stay a review finding.
The manifest does not make the question enforceable; it makes it answerable.

duplicates.reason: the console must compute lineage in the browser with no server, so the rule cannot live only in Python

mutation.why: the flattering drift: report a pre-v3 cell as INDEPENDENT rather than demoting it

rules.history: check_lane_distinctness.py used to re-encode this rule and inverted it: it tested `None` for no-known-derivation while the spec shipped `[]`, so `[] / []` reported as 'one derives from the other'. The fix was deleting the copy, not repairing it. Registered here with zero duplicates so a future re-encoding is a visible change to this file.
